subject: chemistry
title: Relative formula mass and percentage by mass
key_idea: The relative formula mass (Mr) of a compound is the sum of the relative atomic masses (Ar) of all the atoms in its formula. The percentage by mass of an element is its share of the Mr, written as a percentage.

sections.heading: Relative atomic mass and relative formula mass

blocks.text: Atoms are too small to weigh in grams, so chemists compare them using relative masses. This section covers how to work out Mr from a formula.

items.meaning: The average mass of an atom of an element compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It is given in the periodic table.
The sum of the Ar values of all the atoms in the formula of a compound. For a molecule it is also called the relative molecular mass.

blocks.label: Relative formula mass
where: Ar and Mr have no units.
Use the small numbers in the formula to count atoms.
blocks.formula: Mr = sum of the Ar of every atom in the formula

items.text: Mg(OH)₂ has 1 Mg, 2 O and 2 H. The 2 outside the bracket multiplies everything inside.

items: A bracket with a number after it multiplies every atom inside the bracket.
In a balanced equation, the Mr values of the reactants add up to the same total as the Mr values of the products.
If you know the Mr and all the other Ar values, you can find an unknown Ar by subtraction.

items.text: A Group 2 carbonate XCO₃ has Mr = 84. Ar: C = 12, O = 16.
Ar of X = 84 − 60 = 24. X is magnesium.

items: Mr is the sum of the Ar of all the atoms in the formula.
A number outside a bracket multiplies everything inside it.

blocks.text: The percentage by mass tells you how much of a compound's mass is one element. This section covers the calculation and what you can do with it.

blocks.label: Percentage by mass of an element
blocks.formula: percentage by mass = (Ar × number of atoms of the element ÷ Mr of the compound) × 100
where: Ar of the element, from the periodic table.

items.text: Lithium sulfate, Li₂SO₄, has 4 oxygen atoms. 4 × 16 = 64.

items: Use the number of atoms of the element, not just one atom. The answer must be less than 100%.
Check your answer to the number of significant figures the question asks for.

blocks.text: Mass of an element in a sample
Use the same fraction to find the mass of an element in a given mass of compound. Butane, C₄H₁₀, has Mr = 58. Ar: C = 12.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the mass of carbon in a sample of butane.
working: Mass of carbon in one Mr = 4 × 12 = 48
diagram.question: Butane has the formula C₄H₁₀. Its relative formula mass is 58. Calculate the mass of carbon in **{m} g** of butane. (Ar: C = 12)

items: Percentage by mass = (Ar × number of atoms ÷ Mr) × 100.
Multiply the Ar by the number of atoms of that element.
The same fraction gives the mass of an element in a sample.

checks.q: Calculate the relative formula mass of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. (Ar: Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1)
Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in magnesium oxide, MgO. (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16)
Magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂, has Mr = 58. Calculate the percentage by mass of hydrogen in it. (Ar: H = 1)

worked_example.question:
Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in lithium sulfate (Li₂SO₄).

Relative atomic mass (Ar): O = 16

Relative formula mass (Mr): Li₂SO₄ = 110

Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: Marks are given for the mass of oxygen, the fraction, the unrounded value and the rounded answer.

worked_example.question:
Sodium carbonate has the formula Na₂CO₃.

Calculate the percentage by mass of sodium in sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃.

percentage by mass of element = (total relative atomic mass of element ÷ relative formula mass of compound) × 100

(relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
worked_example.tip: The correct answer, 43.4, scores all three marks even without working.

worked_example.question:
Calculate the relative formula mass of a (C₂H₅)₂O molecule.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0
worked_example.tip: Count each type of atom first, then add.

worked_example.question:
Ammonia reacts with an acid to form ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄.

Calculate the percentage composition by mass of nitrogen in (NH₄)₂SO₄.
answer_points: Mass of nitrogen in one formula unit = 2 × 14 = 28
worked_example.tip: One mark for the Mr and one mark for the percentage.

worked_example.question:
Ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄, is used by gardeners as a fertiliser because it contains nitrogen.

Calculate the mass, in grams, of nitrogen in 1.0 kg of ammonium sulfate.

[Mr of (NH₄)₂SO₄ = 132; Ar of N = 14]
answer_points: 132 g of ammonium sulfate contains 28 g of nitrogen
1000 g of ammonium sulfate contains 1000 × (28 ÷ 132) g of nitrogen
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step of the working. Using 14 instead of 28 loses marks, because there are 2 nitrogen atoms in the formula.
